# Standalone script to generate the results for the manuscript figures, tables, text for the field paper, and supplementary materials

#  updated in Sep 2026 dataset that keeps phenology separated by year and tree, so those can be random effects. 

Table of contents
Methods Figs
Fig.1 -  spatial map: impervious surface/land codes

Results Figs
Fig. 2 - intraurban phenological variation -boxplots
Fig. 3 - intraurban phenological variation -spatial
Fig. 4 - frost damage pics
Fig. 5 - scatter plots: temp and phenology
Fig. 6 - scatter plot imp surface / and phenology 
Fig. 7 - bar graphs: land use and phenology

Results text, tables
3.1 Intra-urban phenological variation 
3.2 Abiotic and biotic predictors of tree phenology
3.2.1 Intra-urban temperature relationship with phenology
3.2.2 Impervious surface relationship with phenology
3.2.3 Land-use zones relationships with phenology
3.2.4 Tree size and phenology

3.3 Temperature variation and landscape relationships
3.3.1 Intraurban temperature departures 
3.3.2 Impervious surface, elevation, light, distance to city center  relationship with temperature
3.3.3 Land cover relationship with temperature

Appendix A: Supplementary Data
SM 1. Identification of 'Spring Snow' clones 
SM 2. Map of sites
SM 3. Phenological growth stages
SM 4. Temperature records by site
SM 5. Land-use Zones
SM 6.  Methods for estimating relative light
SM 7. Phenological departure methods and results
SM 8. Tree age and size results
SM 9. Temperature variation results
SM 10. Impervious surface radii results
SM 11. Elevation, light, and distance to city center results
SM 12. Land-use zone results

# Fig. 1 -  spatial map: impervious surface/land codes

```{r impervious surface}
boulder_outline <- sf::st_read("/Users/deidrejaeger/Documents/Career/CU-Boulder/Research/spring-snow-phenology/spatial_data/BoulderCityLimits/BoulderCityLimits.shp")


jul_chill_2021.d.ft <- read.csv(file = "data/chilling_forcing_days/2021/days_to_dyn_chill_ft21.csv")

p.imp <- jul_chill_2021.d.ft %>% 
    ggplot() +  
  geom_sf(data=boulder_outline, 
                 fill=NA,color="grey30", linewidth=0.75) +
    geom_point(aes(x=coords.x1, y=coords.x2, color = pA250),  size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x=coords.x1, y=coords.x2, color = pA250),  size = 3, shape = 1, color = "black") +
    
    scale_color_gradient(low="bisque1", high ="black", name = " Proportion of \n impervious surface\n (250 m radius) \n", limits= c(0,1)) +
    coord_sf() +
    theme_map() +
  labs(tag = "B)") +
    theme(legend.position="right") +
    theme(legend.key.width=unit(1.5, "cm"), 
      legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")) 
p.imp

# 2.# 2.# 2. Save it with a high DPI (e.g., 300 DPI for publication standard)
ggsave("images/Field-manuscript-figs/field-manu-revised-figs/fig.1-imp-surf.png", plot = p.imp, width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```

```{r tree survey years map}
# see if can load this pre-processed dataset from script 20
boulder_outline <- sf::st_read("/Users/deidrejaeger/Documents/Career/CU-Boulder/Research/spring-snow-phenology/spatial_data/BoulderCityLimits/BoulderCityLimits.shp")

df <- read.csv("data/spatial-site-data/spatial_sites.csv")
# create a single set of trees, without the 2019 only trees, and add a site number
df0 <- df %>% 
  select(Site) %>% 
  unique() %>% 
  filter(Site != "WOND", Site != "SUMA",Site != "UNIO",Site != "BAS1") %>% 
  mutate(site_number = seq(1:40))

# join the df and df0
df <- df %>% 
  left_join(df0, by = "Site")

# define color schemes
year_label <- c("2019-2020" = "2019-2021", "2020" = "2020-2021")
year_color <- c( "2019-2020" = "gold4","2020" = "brown")

df.plot <- df %>% 
  filter(year_visit != 2019)

df.labels <- df.plot %>% 
  filter(second.tre != 2)
  
p <- 
  ggplot() +  
   geom_sf(data=boulder_outline,
               fill=NA,color="grey30", linewidth=0.75) +
  geom_point(data = df.plot, aes(x=coords.x1, y=coords.x2, color = year_visit,shape = factor(second.tre)), size = 2) +
   
   geom_label_repel(data = df.labels, aes(x=coords.x1, y=coords.x2, label = site_number),
                  size          = 2,
                  box.padding   = 0.005,
                  label.padding = 0.1,
                  point.padding = 0.1,
                  force         = 35,
                  segment.size  = 0.5,
                  segment.color = "grey50", 
                  direction = c("both", "y", "x"), 
                  min.segment.length = 0.01, 
                  max.overlaps = 15) +
scale_color_manual(name = "Years of survey",
                     labels = year_label,
                     values = year_color) +
   scale_shape_manual(name = "Number of trees per site", 
                      labels = c("1"="1 tree", "2" = "2 trees"),
                      values = c("1" = 19,
                                 "2" = 3)) +
  # annotation_scale() + # this doesn't seem right compared to other plots where 5 km is nearly the whole width of the city
  coord_sf() +
  theme_map() +
   labs(tag = "A)") +
 theme(legend.position="right") +
    theme(legend.key.width=unit(3, "cm"), 
      legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")) 
# theme(legend.key.width=unit(3, "cm")
p

# 2. Save it with a high DPI (e.g., 300 DPI for publication standard)
ggsave("images/Field-manuscript-figs/field-manu-revised-figs/fig.1-tree-sites.png", plot = p, width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```

```{r phenology-anomoly-color-pop-leaves-flowers}
# combine df.4.l and df.4.f

#prep leafout data
df.4.l <- f_t_dat_lo19.21.t %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Site) %>% 
  summarize(jul0.5_tglo = mean(jul0.5_tglo, na.rm = TRUE), jul0.5_TGLO_d_mn = mean(jul0.5_TGLO_d, na.rm = TRUE), jul0.5_TGLO_d_sd = sd(jul0.5_TGLO_d, na.rm = TRUE), average_minTdep_fullyr = mean(average_minTdep_l), coords.x1 = mean(coords.x1), coords.x2 = mean(coords.x2)) %>%
  mutate_all(~ifelse(is.nan(.), NA, .)) %>% 
  mutate(Site = as.factor(Site))


df.4.l.c <- df.4.l %>% 
  mutate(phenophase = "leafout", anomoly_days_m = jul0.5_TGLO_d_mn, anomoly_days_sd = jul0.5_TGLO_d_sd) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Site, phenophase,anomoly_days_m, anomoly_days_sd,average_minTdep_fullyr, coords.x1, coords.x2)

# prep flowering data
# group by site and average across 2019-2021
df.4.f <- f_t_dat_ft19.21.t %>%
  group_by(Site) %>% 
  summarize(jul0.2_tgft = mean(jul0.2_tgft, na.rm = TRUE), jul0.2_TGFT_d_mn = mean(jul0.2_TGFT_d, na.rm = TRUE), jul0.2_TGFT_d_sd = sd(jul0.2_TGFT_d, na.rm = TRUE), average_minTdep_fullyr = mean(average_minTdep_f), coords.x1 = mean(coords.x1), coords.x2 = mean(coords.x2)) %>% 
  mutate_all(~ifelse(is.nan(.), NA, .)) %>% 
  mutate(Site = as.factor(Site))


df.4.f.c <- df.4.f %>% 
  mutate(phenophase = "flowertips", anomoly_days_m = jul0.2_TGFT_d_mn, anomoly_days_sd = jul0.2_TGFT_d_sd) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Site, phenophase,anomoly_days_m, anomoly_days_sd, average_minTdep_fullyr, coords.x1, coords.x2)

# combine
df.4.l.f.c <- rbind(df.4.f.c, df.4.l.c)

#order the phenophase factor levels
df.4.l.f.c$phenophase <- factor(df.4.l.f.c$phenophase, levels= c("leafout", "flowertips"), ordered = TRUE)

# revalue the levels

dataset1 = df.4.l.f.c
colm_interest = "anomoly_days_m"
low_col= "forestgreen"
high_col = "purple"
legend_lab= "Average departure (days)"
lower_lim = -14
upper_lim = 13


 #load outline of boulder

p4.f.c <- dataset1 %>%

    geom_point(data= dataset1, aes(x=coords.x1, y=coords.x2, color = pull(dataset1, colm_interest)), size = 5) +
  geom_point(data= dataset1, aes(x=coords.x1, y=coords.x2),shape = 1, size = 5,colour = "black")+
    scale_colour_gradient2(name = legend_lab, low=low_col, mid = "gray",  high = high_col, midpoint=0, limits= c(lower_lim, upper_lim), expand = c(0,0), breaks = seq(lower_lim, upper_lim, 2)) +
```

# Fig 5 temp and phenology

```{r LMEM leaves - temp - SIG}

library(lme4) # for lmer
library(lmerTest) # for lmer p values based on degrees of freedom
library(DHARMa)        # simulation-based residual checks (very good for mixed models)
library(performance)

f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/leafout-temp-dep-2019-20-21.revise.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# make site a factor
f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site <- as.factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site)

f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/leaf-predictors.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Tree = SSS.tag_as, Year = year)

# preapare gounping variables
# make site a factor
f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site <- as.factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site) 
f_t_dat_lo19.21$Year <- as.factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$Year)

# temp NO REML , use maximum likihood (ML)
lo.mixed.tl<- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.5_TGLO_d ~  average_minTdep_l + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = f_t_dat_lo19.21)

library(ggeffects)
library(lme4)
# plot the model with ggpredict
# left off here Thursday

# plot fixed effects
predictions <- ggpredict(
  lo.mixed.tl, # lnear mixed effects model outcome
  terms = c("average_minTdep_l"),  # fixed effects
  type = "fixed") # include random effect variance (if not specifics, assumes no random effects)



# reorder zone levels
f_t_dat_lo19.21$zone_nam_1<- factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$zone_nam_1, levels= c("Business-district", 
                            "Residential-high",
                           "Residential-med",
                           "Residential-low",
                           "Park"))

# load zones
zone_names <- c("Business-district" = "Business-district", 
                "Residential-high" = "Residential-high", 
                "Residential-med" = "Residential-med", 
                "Residential-low" = "Residential-low", 
                "Park" = "Park")

zone_colors <- c("Business-district" = "orange", 
                 "Residential-high" = "pink", 
                 "Residential-med" = "yellow", 
                 "Residential-low" = "green", 
                 "Park" = "darkgreen")
```

```{r LMEM - temp pheno interaction panel}
library(lme4)
library(ggeffects)
library(ggplot2)
# look at how leaves and flowers are affect by temperature

#  load data
f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/leafout-temp-dep-2019-20-21.revise.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

f_t_dat_ft19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/flower-tip-temp-dep-2019-20-21.revise.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# create a shared dataset with departures
leaves <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
  mutate(departure.p = jul0.5_TGLO_d, departure.t = average_minTdep_l, phenophase = "Leaf opening") %>% 
    select(Site, SSS.tag_as, year , phenophase,  departure.p, departure.t) 

flowers <- f_t_dat_ft19.21 %>% 
   mutate(departure.p = jul0.2_TGFT_d, departure.t = average_minTdep_f, phenophase = "Flower emergence") %>% 
    select(Site, SSS.tag_as, year, phenophase, departure.p, departure.t) 

# link rows
l.f.t.int <- flowers %>% 
  rbind(leaves) %>% 
dplyr::rename(Tree = SSS.tag_as, Year = year)

#reorder zone levels
l.f.t.int$phenophase<- factor(l.f.t.int$phenophase, levels= c("Leaf opening", 
                            "Flower emergence"))

# check col names
colnames(flowers) == colnames(leaves)


# look at how temp predicts phenolody with phenophase and interaction of temp on phenophase
l.f.t.int.m <- lmerTest::lmer(departure.p ~ departure.t + phenophase + phenophase*departure.t + (1|Year) + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = l.f.t.int)
summary(l.f.t.int.m)
l.f.t.int.m

 # 2. Calculate the predicted values for the interaction
# Syntax: terms = c("continuous_var", "categorical_var")
predictions <- predict_response(l.f.t.int.m, terms = c("departure.t", "phenophase"))



# 3. Plot using the built-in ggplot wrapper
# Create a named vector of colors for your factor levels
my_colors <- c("Leaf opening" = "steelblue3", "Flower emergence" = "seagreen")

int.tp.plot <- plot(predictions) +
  labs(title = " ",
    x = "Temperature departure (°C)",
    y = "Departure (days)") +
  scale_color_manual(values = my_colors) + 
 theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),  
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14), 
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14),  
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14), 
      legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")) + 
  labs(color = "Phenophase") + 
    labs(tag = "C)") 
int.tp.plot 
```

```{r grid-leaf-flower-pheno-temp-graph}
# phen.t <- p.3.l / p.3.f + plot_layout(guides = "collect")

# grid.arrange(p.3.l, p.3.f,ncol = 1, nrow = 2)

pheno.t2 <- p.3.l / p.3.f / int.tp.plot 

# 2. Save it with a high DPI (e.g., 300 DPI for publication standard)
ggsave("images/Field-manuscript-figs/field-manu-revised-figs/fig.5-t-phen-interaction.png", plot = pheno.t2, width = 6, height =8, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```

# 3.2 Predictors of tree phenology
## Intra-urban temperature relationship with phenology 

```{r LMEM leaves - temp - SIG}

library(lme4) # for lmer
library(lmerTest) # for lmer p values based on degrees of freedom
library(DHARMa)        # simulation-based residual checks (very good for mixed models)
library(performance)


f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/leaf-predictors.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Tree = SSS.tag_as, Year = year)

# preapare gounping variables
# make site a factor
f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site <- as.factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site) 
f_t_dat_lo19.21$Year <- as.factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$Year)

# YEAR SHOWED no variation as a random effect, so dropped
# # temp NO REML , use maximum likihood (ML)
# lo.mixed.tl<- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.5_TGLO_d ~  average_minTdep_l + (1 | Year) + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = f_t_dat_lo19.21)
# lo.mixed.tl
# summary(lo.mixed.tl)

# temp WITH YEAR  , use maximum likihood (ML)
lo.mixed.tl<- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.5_TGLO_d ~  average_minTdep_l + (1| Year) + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = f_t_dat_lo19.21)
lo.mixed.tl
summary(lo.mixed.tl)
# temp NO REML , use maximum likihood (ML)
lo.mixed.tl<- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.5_TGLO_d ~  average_minTdep_l + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = f_t_dat_lo19.21)
lo.mixed.tl
summary(lo.mixed.tl)

# see slope. The estimate is the Slope, which is the average change in the dependent variable (leaf open) for every one unit increase in the independent variable (temp). So for every 1 degree increase in average temp departure, leaf burst is 3.17 days earlier. 

VarCorr(lo.mixed.tl)

# Residuals vs fitted — look for no pattern, constant spread
plot(lo.mixed.tl)

# Q-Q plot of residuals — check normality - some S tailed a bit
qqnorm(resid(lo.mixed.tl)); qqline(resid(lo.mixed.tl))

# Use dharma to simulate residuals
sim_res.l <- simulateResiduals(lo.mixed.tl, allow.new.levels = TRUE)
plot(sim_res.l)

# Specific tests
testDispersion(sim_res.l)
testOutliers(sim_res.l) #significant. We should Test if dropping the outliers and see if we get a similare result


# can calculate the proportion of total variance attributable to each grouping level, to say X % of the variation in budburst timing that isn't explained by temp is due to the differences between sites, versus 15% duue to differences between trees within a site.
vc.l <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(lo.mixed.tl))
vc.l$vcov / sum(vc.l$vcov)   # proportion of variance per component

# use performance package to calculate a marginal and conditional r2
performance::r2(lo.mixed.tl)
# Marginal R²: variance explained by fixed effects only (temperature)
#Conditional R²: variance explained by fixed + random effects together

# The gap between them tells you how much of your model's explanatory power comes from the site/tree structure versus temperature itself.


AIC(lo.mixed.tl) # lower AIC better, When you fit a linear mixed-effects model, R defaults to REML (Restricted Maximum Likelihood) estimation because it provides unbiased estimates for variance components. However, you cannot compare AIC values between models with different fixed effects if they are fitted using REML.If you are comparing models with different fixed effect structures, you must set REML = FALSE (or use Maximum Likelihood, method = "ML") in your model function
```

```{r temp without outliers - still SIG}
f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/leaf-predictors.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
  rename(Tree = SSS.tag_as, Year = year)

# preapare gounping variables
# make site a factor
f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site <- as.factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site) 
f_t_dat_lo19.21$Year <- as.factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$Year)


f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
  filter(!is.na(average_minTdep_l) , !is.na(jul0.5_TGLO_d))

# temp NO REML , use maximum likihood (ML)
lo.mixed.tl<- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.5_TGLO_d ~  average_minTdep_l + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = f_t_dat_lo19.21)
lo.mixed.tl
summary(lo.mixed.tl)

# Extract standardized or Pearson residuals
f_t_dat_lo19.21$resid <- residuals(lo.mixed.tl, type = "pearson")

# Identify rows where residuals exceed 3 standard deviations
outliers <- abs(f_t_dat_lo19.21$resid) > 3

# Filter out the outlier rows
clean_data <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% filter(!outliers)

# Refit the mixed-effect model
no_outlier.tm <- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.5_TGLO_d ~  average_minTdep_l + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = clean_data)

no_outlier.tm 


summary(no_outlier.tm)

VarCorr(no_outlier.tm)

# Residuals vs fitted — look for no pattern, constant spread
plot(no_outlier.tm)

# Q-Q plot of residuals — check normality - some S tailed a bit
qqnorm(resid(no_outlier.tm)); qqline(resid(no_outlier.tm))

# Use dharma to simulate residuals
sim_res.l <- simulateResiduals(no_outlier.tm, allow.new.levels = TRUE)
plot(sim_res.l)


# Use dharma to simulate residuals
sim_res.l <- simulateResiduals(lo.mixed.tl, allow.new.levels = TRUE)
plot(sim_res.l)
# Specific tests
testDispersion(sim_res.l)
testOutliers(sim_res.l) #significant. We should Test if dropping the outliers and see if we get a similare result


# can calculate the proportion of total variance attributable to each grouping level, to say X % of the variation in budburst timing that isn't explained by temp is due to the differences between sites, versus 15% duue to differences between trees within a site.
vc.l <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(no_outlier.tm))
vc.l$vcov / sum(vc.l$vcov)   # proportion of variance per component

# use performance package to calculate a marginal and conditional r2
performance::r2(no_outlier.tm)
# Marginal R²: variance explained by fixed effects only (temperature)
#Conditional R²: variance explained by fixed + random effects together

# The gap between them tells you how much of your model's explanatory power comes from the site/tree structure versus temperature itself.


AIC(no_outlier.tm) # lower AIC #470
```

```{r LMEM flowers- temp - SIG}

library(lme4) # for lmer
library(lmerTest) # for lmer p values based on degrees of freedom
library(DHARMa)        # simulation-based residual checks (very good for mixed models)
library(performance)

# prep flower data

f_t_dat_ft19.21  <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/flower-predictors.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

f_t_dat_ft19.21  <- f_t_dat_ft19.21 %>% 
  rename(Tree = SSS.tag_as, Year = year)

# preapare gounping variables
# make site a factor
f_t_dat_ft19.21$Site <- as.factor(f_t_dat_ft19.21$Site) 
f_t_dat_ft19.21$Year <- as.factor(f_t_dat_ft19.21$Year)

# fl.mixed <- lmer(y ~ x + (1 | group), data = my_data)
fl.mixed <- lmer(jul0.2_TGFT_d ~ average_minTdep_f + (1| Year) + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree), data = f_t_dat_ft19.21)

fl.mixed
summary(fl.mixed)

VarCorr(fl.mixed)

# interpretation: 
# Site variance: how much budburst timing varies between sites, after accounting for temperature. Large relative to Tree:Site → site-level factors (soil, microclimate, elevation) matter a lot.
 # in our case, the site explains more than the tree in a site, but not a ton more after accounting for temp. 
# Tree:Site variance: how much individual trees differ from each other within the same site. Large relative to Site → individual tree genetics/exposure matter more than which site they're in.
# Residual variance: leftover variation not explained by site, tree, or temperature — includes year-to-year noise, measurement error, unmeasured factors.

# Residuals vs fitted — look for no pattern, constant spread
plot(fl.mixed)

# Q-Q plot of residuals — check normality - some S tailed a bit
qqnorm(resid(fl.mixed)); qqline(resid(fl.mixed))

#  the smallest and largest observations (left-hand and right-hand sides of the QQ-plot, respectively) have an s-tail, 
# the smallest observations are smaller than you would expect from a normal distribution (i.e. the points are below the line on the QQ-plot). This means the lower tail of the data’s distribution has beenextended, relative to a normal distribution.
# the largest observations are larger than you would expect from a normal distribution (i.e. the points are above the line on the QQ-plot). This means the upper tail of the data’s distribution has beenextended, relative to a normal distribution (https://www.ucd.ie/ecomodel/resources/examplesofquantile-quantileplots/)

# Use dharma to simulate residuals
sim_res <- simulateResiduals(fl.mixed)
plot(fl.mixed)

# Specific tests
# # Test for overdispersion or underdispersion
# Simulation-based: It compares the standard deviation (or variance) of the observed scaled quantile residuals against the standard deviation of residuals generated from data simulated under the fitted model.Nonparametric: It avoids strict distributional or asymptotic assumptions by relying purely on the simulated residual distributions.Interpretation: A dispersion statistic close to 1.0 indicates proper dispersion (equidispersion), whereas values significantly greater than 1 suggest overdispersion (excess variance), and values lower than 1 suggest underdispersion. The accompanying p-value tests whether this deviation is statistically significant.

testDispersion(sim_res)
# not sig , so not over/unde dispersed


testOutliers(sim_res)
# sig outlier


# can calculate the proportion of total variance attributable to each grouping level, to say X % of the variation in budburst timing that isn't explained by temp is due to the differences between sites, versus 15% duue to differences between trees within a site.
vc.f <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fl.mixed))
vc.f$vcov / sum(vc.f$vcov)   # proportion of variance per component

# use performance package to calculate a marginal and conditional r2
performance::r2(fl.mixed)

# Marginal R²: variance explained by fixed effects only (temperature)
#Conditional R²: variance explained by fixed + random effects together

# The gap between them tells you how much of your model's explanatory power comes from the site/tree structure versus temperature itself.

AIC(fl.mixed) # lower AIC better, When you fit a linear mixed-effects model, R defaults to REML (Restricted Maximum Likelihood) estimation because it provides unbiased estimates for variance components. However, you cannot compare AIC values between models with different fixed effects if they are fitted using REML.If you are comparing models with different fixed effect structures, you must set REML = FALSE (or use Maximum Likelihood, method = "ML") in your model function
```

```{r flower temp without outliers - still SIG}
# prep flower data

f_t_dat_ft19.21  <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/flower-predictors.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

f_t_dat_ft19.21  <- f_t_dat_ft19.21 %>% 
  rename(Tree = SSS.tag_as, Year = year)

# preapare gounping variables
# make site a factor
f_t_dat_ft19.21$Site <- as.factor(f_t_dat_ft19.21$Site) 
f_t_dat_ft19.21$Year <- as.factor(f_t_dat_ft19.21$Year)


f_t_dat_ft19.21 <- f_t_dat_ft19.21 %>% 
  filter(!is.na(average_minTdep_f) , !is.na(jul0.2_TGFT_d))

# temp NO REML , use maximum likihood (ML)
fl.mixed.tl<- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.2_TGFT_d ~  average_minTdep_f + (1 | Year) + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = f_t_dat_ft19.21)
fl.mixed.tl
summary(fl.mixed.tl)

# Extract standardized or Pearson residuals
f_t_dat_ft19.21$resid <- residuals(fl.mixed.tl, type = "pearson")

# Identify rows where residuals exceed 3 standard deviations
outliers <- abs(f_t_dat_ft19.21$resid) > 3

# Filter out the outlier rows
clean_data <- f_t_dat_ft19.21 %>% filter(!outliers)

# Refit the mixed-effect model
no_outlier.tm <- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.2_TGFT_d ~  average_minTdep_f +(1 | Year) +  (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = clean_data)

no_outlier.tm 


summary(no_outlier.tm)

VarCorr(no_outlier.tm)

# Residuals vs fitted — look for no pattern, constant spread
plot(no_outlier.tm)

# Q-Q plot of residuals — check normality - some S tailed a bit
qqnorm(resid(no_outlier.tm)); qqline(resid(no_outlier.tm))

# Use dharma to simulate residuals
sim_res.l <- simulateResiduals(no_outlier.tm, allow.new.levels = TRUE)
plot(sim_res.l)


# Use dharma to simulate residuals
sim_res.l <- simulateResiduals(no_outlier.tm, allow.new.levels = TRUE)
plot(sim_res.l)
# Specific tests
testDispersion(sim_res.l)
testOutliers(sim_res.l) #significant. We should Test if dropping the outliers and see if we get a similare result


# can calculate the proportion of total variance attributable to each grouping level, to say X % of the variation in budburst timing that isn't explained by temp is due to the differences between sites, versus 15% duue to differences between trees within a site.
vc.l <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(no_outlier.tm))
vc.l$vcov / sum(vc.l$vcov)   # proportion of variance per component

# use performance package to calculate a marginal and conditional r2
performance::r2(no_outlier.tm)
# Marginal R²: variance explained by fixed effects only (temperature)
#Conditional R²: variance explained by fixed + random effects together

# The gap between them tells you how much of your model's explanatory power comes from the site/tree structure versus temperature itself.


AIC(no_outlier.tm) # A LOT lower AIC #317

```

```{r LMEM interaction between phenophase-temp}
library(lme4)
library(ggeffects)
library(ggplot2)
# look at how leaves and flowers are affect by temperature

#  load data
f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/leafout-temp-dep-2019-20-21.revise.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

f_t_dat_ft19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/flower-tip-temp-dep-2019-20-21.revise.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# create a shared dataset with departures
leaves <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
  mutate(departure.p = jul0.5_TGLO_d, departure.t = average_minTdep_l, phenophase = "Leaf opening") %>% 
    select(Site, SSS.tag_as, year , phenophase,  departure.p, departure.t) 

flowers <- f_t_dat_ft19.21 %>% 
   mutate(departure.p = jul0.2_TGFT_d, departure.t = average_minTdep_f, phenophase = "Flower emergence") %>% 
    select(Site, SSS.tag_as, year, phenophase, departure.p, departure.t) 

# link rows
l.f.t.int <- flowers %>% 
  rbind(leaves) %>% 
dplyr::rename(Tree = SSS.tag_as, Year = year)

#reorder zone levels
l.f.t.int$phenophase<- factor(l.f.t.int$phenophase, levels= c("Leaf opening", 
                            "Flower emergence"))

# check col names
colnames(flowers) == colnames(leaves)


# look at how temp predicts phenolody with phenophase and interaction of temp on phenophase
l.f.t.int.m <- lmerTest::lmer(departure.p ~ departure.t + phenophase + phenophase*departure.t + (1|Year) + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = l.f.t.int)
summary(l.f.t.int.m)
l.f.t.int.m

# create table
sjPlot::tab_model(l.f.t.int.m,
                                  # 1. Custom predictor labels (must align with the order of coefficients)
  pred.labels = c("(Intercept)", "Temperature departure (°C)", "Phenophase", "Temperature departure (°C) x Phenophase"),

  # 2. Custom dependent variable label
  dv.labels = c("Phenology departures (days)"),
  show.aic = F,

  # 3. Prevent sjPlot from trying to auto-fetch labels from data attributes
  auto.label = FALSE
)
```

## Impervious surface relationship with phenology
```{r LMEM leaves - imp - SIG}

library(lme4) # for lmer
library(lmerTest) # for lmer p values based on degrees of freedom
library(DHARMa)        # simulation-based residual checks (very good for mixed models)
library(performance)


f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/leaf-predictors.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
  rename(Tree = SSS.tag_as, Year = year)

# preapare gounping variables
# make site a factor
f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site <- as.factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site) 
f_t_dat_lo19.21$Year <- as.factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$Year)

# remove wonderland, union, bas1, 
f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
   filter(Site != "WOND", Site != "SUMA",Site != "UNIO",Site != "BAS1") 

# YEAR and Tree and Site SHOWED no variation as a random effect, so dropped
# temp NO REML , use maximum likihood (ML)
lo.mixed.tl.1<- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.5_TGLO_d ~  pA250  + (1 | Year) + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = f_t_dat_lo19.21)
lo.mixed.tl.1
summary(lo.mixed.tl.1)


# temp NO REML , use maximum likihood (ML)
lo.mixed.tl<- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.5_TGLO_d ~  pA250 + (1 | Site) , REML =  FALSE, data = f_t_dat_lo19.21)
lo.mixed.tl
summary(lo.mixed.tl)

# see slope. The estimate is the Slope, which is the average change in the dependent variable (leaf open) for every one unit increase in the independent variable (temp). So for every 1 degree increase in average temp departure, leaf burst is 3.17 days earlier. 

VarCorr(lo.mixed.tl)

# Residuals vs fitted — look for no pattern, constant spread
plot(lo.mixed.tl)

# Q-Q plot of residuals — check normality - some S tailed a bit
qqnorm(resid(lo.mixed.tl)); qqline(resid(lo.mixed.tl))

# Use dharma to simulate residuals
sim_res.l <- simulateResiduals(lo.mixed.tl, allow.new.levels = TRUE)
plot(sim_res.l)

# Specific tests
testDispersion(sim_res.l)
testOutliers(sim_res.l) #significant. We should Test if dropping the outliers and see if we get a similare result


# can calculate the proportion of total variance attributable to each grouping level, to say X % of the variation in budburst timing that isn't explained by temp is due to the differences between sites, versus 15% duue to differences between trees within a site.
vc.l <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(lo.mixed.tl))
vc.l$vcov / sum(vc.l$vcov)   # proportion of variance per component

# use performance package to calculate a marginal and conditional r2
performance::r2(lo.mixed.tl)
# Marginal R²: variance explained by fixed effects only (temperature)
#Conditional R²: variance explained by fixed + random effects together

# The gap between them tells you how much of your model's explanatory power comes from the site/tree structure versus temperature itself.


AIC(lo.mixed.tl) # lower AIC better, When you fit a linear mixed-effects model, R defaults to REML (Restricted Maximum Likelihood) estimation because it provides unbiased estimates for variance components. However, you cannot compare AIC values between models with different fixed effects if they are fitted using REML.If you are comparing models with different fixed effect structures, you must set REML = FALSE (or use Maximum Likelihood, method = "ML") in your model function
```

```{r LMEM flowers- imp- SIG}
# Simulation-based: It compares the standard deviation (or variance) of the observed scaled quantile residuals against the standard deviation of residuals generated from data simulated under the fitted model.Nonparametric: It avoids strict distributional or asymptotic assumptions by relying purely on the simulated residual distributions.Interpretation: A dispersion statistic close to 1.0 indicates proper dispersion (equidispersion), whereas values significantly greater than 1 suggest overdispersion (excess variance), and values lower than 1 suggest underdispersion. The accompanying p-value tests whether this deviation is statistically significant.

testDispersion(sim_res)
# not sig , so not over/unde dispersed


testOutliers(sim_res)
# sig outlier


# can calculate the proportion of total variance attributable to each grouping level, to say X % of the variation in budburst timing that isn't explained by temp is due to the differences between sites, versus 15% duue to differences between trees within a site.
vc.f <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fl.mixed))
vc.f$vcov / sum(vc.f$vcov)   # proportion of variance per component

# use performance package to calculate a marginal and conditional r2
performance::r2(fl.mixed)

# Marginal R²: variance explained by fixed effects only (temperature)
#Conditional R²: variance explained by fixed + random effects together

# The gap between them tells you how much of your model's explanatory power comes from the site/tree structure versus temperature itself.

AIC(fl.mixed) # lower AIC better, When you fit a linear mixed-effects model, R defaults to REML (Restricted Maximum Likelihood) estimation because it provides unbiased estimates for variance components. However, you cannot compare AIC values between models with different fixed effects if they are fitted using REML.If you are comparing models with different fixed effect structures, you must set REML = FALSE (or use Maximum Likelihood, method = "ML") in your model function
```

```{r zone LMEM leaves - SIG }
# set levels ()
#reorder zone levels
f_t_dat_lo19.21$zone_nam_1 <- factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$zone_nam_1, levels= c("Business-district", 
                            "Residential-high",
                           "Residential-med",
                           "Residential-low",
                           "Park"))



# remove wonderland, union, bas1, 
f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
   filter(Site != "WOND", Site != "SUMA",Site != "UNIO",Site != "BAS1") 

# # ANOVA land use zone Year and tree at a site have no variation, so not including
# lo.mixed.4<- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.5_TGLO_d ~ zone_nam_1 + (1| Year) + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree), REML =  FALSE, data = f_t_dat_lo19.21)
# lo.mixed.4
# summary(lo.mixed.4)

# ANOVA land use zone
lo.mixed.4<- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.5_TGLO_d ~ zone_nam_1 + (1 | Site), REML =  FALSE, data = f_t_dat_lo19.21)
lo.mixed.4
summary(lo.mixed.4)

## S3 method for class 'merMod'
model_performance(
  lo.mixed.4,
  metrics = "all",
  estimator = "ML",
  verbose = TRUE
)

performance_aic(lo.mixed.4, estimator = "ML")

library(sjmisc)
library(sjlabelled)
library(performance)

sjPlot::tab_model(lo.mixed.4,
                                  # 1. Custom predictor labels (must align with the order of coefficients)
  pred.labels = c("(Intercept)", "Business district:Park", "Business district:Res. high","Business district:Res. low","Business district:Res. med"),

  # 2. Custom dependent variable label
  dv.labels = "leaf opening",
  show.aic = TRUE,
string.ci = "CI",
  # 3. Prevent sjPlot from trying to auto-fetch labels from data attributes
  auto.label = FALSE
)


performance_aic(lo.mixed.4, estimator = "ML") # have to manually add this in

VarCorr(lo.mixed.4)

# Residuals vs fitted — look for no pattern, constant spread
plot(lo.mixed.4)

# Q-Q plot of residuals — check normality - some S tailed a bit
qqnorm(resid(lo.mixed.4)); qqline(lo.mixed.4)

# Use dharma to simulate residuals
sim_res.l <- simulateResiduals(lo.mixed.4, allow.new.levels = TRUE)
plot(sim_res.l) # The spread or dispersion of your scaled residuals differs significantly between at least one pair of groups.


# # this might be showing a more complex structure than lme can handle
#  Users often find that glmmTMB is less prone to singular fit or convergence warnings compared to lme4 under difficult data conditions. lme4 (lmer) uses REML by default for linear models, whereas glmmTMB uses Maximum Likelihood (ML) by default for all models. This can lead to slightly different AIC or log-likelihood values unless explicitly aligned. Choose glmmTMB if: You have zero-inflated data, overdispersion, custom correlation structures (autoregressive, spatial), or if lme4 throws persistent convergence errors or singular boundary warnings

# Specific tests
testDispersion(sim_res.l)
testOutliers(sim_res.l)


# can calculate the proportion of total variance attributable to each grouping level, to say X % of the variation in budburst timing that isn't explained by temp is due to the differences between sites, versus 15% duue to differences between trees within a site.
vc.l <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(lo.mixed.4))
vc.l$vcov / sum(vc.l$vcov)   # proportion of variance per component

# use performance package to calculate a marginal and conditional r2
performance::r2(lo.mixed.4)
# Marginal R²: variance explained by fixed effects only (temperature)
#Conditional R²: variance explained by fixed + random effects together

# The gap between them tells you how much of your model's explanatory power comes from the site/tree structure versus temperature itself.


AIC(lo.mixed.4) # lower AIC better, # 859



# look at the post hoc test

# install.packages("emmeans")
library(emmeans)
library(lme4)


mod.emm <- emmeans(lo.mixed.4, ~ zone_nam_1)
mod.emm
pairwise = pairs(mod.emm, simple="zone_nam_1",adjust="tukey")
pairwise

# 3. Extract the pairwise contrasts into a standard data frame
pairwise_df <- as.data.frame(pairwise)


library(gt)

pairwise_df %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Post-Hoc Pairwise Comparisons",
    subtitle = "Adjusted via Tukey's HSD method"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(estimate, SE, t.ratio),
    decimals = 3
  ) %>%
  fmt_scientific(
    columns = p.value,
    rows = p.value < 0.001
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    contrast = "Comparison",
    estimate = "Difference",
    SE = "Std. Error",
    df = "df",
    t.ratio = "t",
    p.value = "p-value"
  )

```

```{r temp-proxy-factors-sites}
# In a random effects or mixed-effects model table, ICC stands for the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient, which measures the proportion of total outcome variance that lies between groups or clusters rather than within them
```

From reviewer 2: The relationship between leaf opening and flower emergence should also be analyzed directly, especially because both phenophases were measured on the same trees. 

```{r LMEM-leaves-flowers direct relationship}

# look at how leaves and flowers are correlated

#  load data
f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/leafout-temp-dep-2019-20-21.revise.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

f_t_dat_ft19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/flower-tip-temp-dep-2019-20-21.revise.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# create a shared dataset with departures
leaves <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
  select(jul0.5_TGLO_d, SSS.tag_as, year, Site) %>% 
  mutate(join = paste(SSS.tag_as, year, sep = "-"))

flowers <- f_t_dat_ft19.21 %>% 
  select(jul0.2_TGFT_d, SSS.tag_as, year, Site) %>% 
   mutate(join = paste(SSS.tag_as, year, sep = "-"))

# link 
l.f.cor <- flowers %>% 
  left_join(leaves, by = "join")

l.f.cor <- l.f.cor %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Tree = SSS.tag_as.x, Year = year.x, Site = Site.x) %>% 
   filter(Site != "WOND", Site != "SUMA",Site != "UNIO", Site != "BAS1") 
# preapare gounping variables
# make site a factor
l.f.cor$Site <- as.factor(l.f.cor$Site) 
l.f.cor$Year <- as.factor(l.f.cor$Year)


# Direct relationship between leaves and flowers - leaves not predictive of flowers
# temp NO REML , use maximum likihood (ML)
lo.mixed.tl <- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.2_TGFT_d ~ jul0.5_TGLO_d + (1|Year) + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree) , REML =  FALSE, data = l.f.cor)


summary(lo.mixed.tl)

# table of this model
sjPlot::tab_model(lo.mixed.tl,
                                  # 1. Custom predictor labels (must align with the order of coefficients)
  pred.labels = c("(Intercept)", "Leaf opening \n departure (days)"),

  # 2. Custom dependent variable label
  dv.labels = " Flower emergence (days)",
    show.aic = F,

  # 3. Prevent sjPlot from trying to auto-fetch labels from data attributes
  auto.label = FALSE
)

```

```{r panels}

# min temp (all months)
lm.500 <- lm(average_minTdep_fullyr~pA500, data = lo_imp.d)
summary(lm.500) # r squared 0.4852 - most highly correlated


# Regression intervals:
# create a dataframe to store predictions of the budburst date
newd.4 <- data.frame(pA500 = rep(seq(min(lo_imp.d$pA500), max(lo_imp.d$pA500), length.out=100),1))
# store predictions from lm model
preds <- predict(lm.500,newdata=newd.4,se.fit=TRUE)
mnlp <- preds$fit        #mean of the linear predictor
selp <- preds$se.fit     #se of the linear predictor
cillp <- mnlp - 2 * selp #lower of 95% CI for linear predictor
ciulp <- mnlp + 2 * selp #upper

# gather predictions into a data frame, 
preds <- cbind(newd.4,preds,cillp,ciulp,mnlp)



# plot the regression no lines

                alpha=0.2,color = "gray", fill = "gray", data=preds) +
    geom_line(mapping=aes(x=pA500,y=mnlp), color = "black", data=preds) +
ylab("Temperature departure (°C)") +

# min temp (all months)
lm.10 <- lm(average_minTdep_fullyr~pA10, data = lo_imp.d)

# Regression intervals:
# create a dataframe to store predictions of the budburst date
newd.4 <- data.frame(pA10 = rep(seq(min(lo_imp.d$pA10), max(lo_imp.d$pA10), length.out=100),1))
# store predictions from lm model
preds <- predict(lm.10,newdata=newd.4,se.fit=TRUE)
mnlp <- preds$fit        #mean of the linear predictor
selp <- preds$se.fit     #se of the linear predictor
cillp <- mnlp - 2 * selp #lower of 95% CI for linear predictor
ciulp <- mnlp + 2 * selp #upper

# gather predictions into a data frame, 
preds <- cbind(newd.4,preds,cillp,ciulp,mnlp)

# plot the regression no lines

  annotate(
```

# SM 2.4. Land-use zone results 

```{r summarize -sd-se-functions}
#+++++++++++++++++++++++++
# Function to calculate the mean and the standard deviation
  # for each group
#+++++++++++++++++++++++++
# data : a data frame
# varname : the name of a column containing the variable
  #to be summariezed
# groupnames : vector of column names to be used as
  # grouping variables
data_summary.se <- function(data, varname, groupnames){
  calcSE <- function(x){sd(x)/sqrt(length(x))}
  
  require(plyr)
  summary_func <- function(x, col){
    c(mean = mean(x[[col]], na.rm=TRUE),
      se = calcSE(x[[col]]),
      sd = sd(x[[col]], na.rm=TRUE))
  }
  data_sum<-ddply(data, groupnames, .fun=summary_func,
                  varname)
  data_sum <- rename(data_sum, c("mean" = varname))
  
 return(data_sum)
}
```

```{r -barplot function -imp surface}
pre.post_barplot.se.i <- function(dataset, question, grouping.col ) {
  
  #### function to create a bar plot with errors bars shaowing the standard deviation (spread of data)
  # dataset is a dataframe that needs to have a grouping column ( ex: in prepost data this is type with levels pre and post)
  # question should be the column name for a particular questions, in quotes
  # grouping.col should be the column with the 2 levels, in quotes
  # returns a bar plot of pre/post data
  
mean.se.sd.summary <- data_summary.se(data = dataset, varname = question, groupnames = grouping.col)
names(mean.se.sd.summary)[1] <- "levels"
names(mean.se.sd.summary)[2] <- "mean"
names(mean.se.sd.summary)[3] <- "se"
names(mean.se.sd.summary)[4] <- "sd"

fill.colors <- c("orange", "pink", "yellow", "springgreen", "darkgreen")

  p.1 <- ggplot(data = mean.se.sd.summary, aes(x= levels, y = mean, fill = levels)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill.colors) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", 
  position=position_dodge()) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-se, ymax=mean+se), width=.2,
                 position=position_dodge(.9)) +
  ylab("Impervious surface proportion (250 m radius)") + 
    xlab("Land-use zone") +
    theme_classic()+
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
  return(p.1)
}


```

```{r load dataset}
# load imp surface data
imp_s <- read.csv(file = "data/paige_analysis/light_impervious_surf_radii_by_site.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


lo_d <- read.csv(file = "data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/leafout-temp-dep-2019-20-21.by-site.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE) #this is not opening properly 1/25/2022 but was the 

temp.site <- lo_d %>% 
  dplyr::select(average_minTdep_fullyr, Site, zone_nam_1) %>% 
  distinct()


# calc the mean in squared to feet, 1 meter = 3.28 feet
imp_s.s <- imp_s %>% 
  group_by(Site) %>% 
  summarize( tot_500m.s = (mean(tot_500m, na.rm = TRUE)), tot_250m.s = (mean(tot_250m, na.rm = TRUE)), tot_150m.s = (mean(tot_150m, na.rm = TRUE)), tot_50m.s = (mean(tot_50m, na.rm = TRUE)), tot_25m.s = (mean(tot_25m, na.rm = TRUE)), tot_10m.s = (mean(tot_10m, na.rm = TRUE))) 

# merge data
lo_imp.d<- temp.site %>% 
  left_join(imp_s.s, by = "Site")

# calc the proportion of imp surface out of the radius in  FEET
# add the totoal area for each radii
lo_imp.d <- lo_imp.d %>% 
  mutate(totA_10 = 3381.9, totA_25 = 21134.4, totA_50 = 84537.5, totA_150 = 760775.6, totA_250 = 2113437.5, totA_500 = 8453749.9) 

# calc the proportion of imp surface out of the radius in  FEET
# add the totoal area for each radii
lo_imp.d <- lo_imp.d %>% 
  mutate(totA_10 = 3381.9, totA_25 = 21134.4, totA_50 = 84537.5, totA_150 = 760775.6, totA_250 = 2113437.5, totA_500 = 8453749.9) 

# calc the proportions
lo_imp.d <- lo_imp.d %>% 
  mutate(pA10 = (tot_10m.s/totA_10), pA25 = (tot_25m.s/totA_25), pA50 = (tot_50m.s/totA_50), pA150 = (tot_150m.s/totA_150), pA250 = (tot_250m.s/totA_250), pA500 = (tot_500m.s/totA_500))

 # change NaN to NA so it doest mess up the calculations later on

  # change NaN to NA so it doest mess up the calculations later on
lo_imp.d$pA25[is.nan(lo_imp.d$pA25)]<-NA
  # change NaN to NA so it doest mess up the calculations later on
lo_imp.d$pA50[is.nan(lo_imp.d$pA50)]<-NA

lo_imp.d$pA150 <- as.numeric(lo_imp.d$pA150)

#reorder zone levels

                            "Residential-high",
                           "Residential-med",
                           "Residential-low",

                  "Residential-high" = "Residential-high", 
                  "Residential-med" = "Residential-med",
```

```{r light spatial plot}
               fill=NA,color="black", size=0.5) +
  scale_color_gradient2(low="black", mid="gray", high ="orange", midpoint = (min(df$rel_light_site)+ ((max(df$rel_light_site)-min(df$rel_light_site))/2)), limits = c(min(df$rel_light_site), max(df$rel_light_site))) +
                        # breaks = c(1575, 1600, 1625, 1650, 1675, 1700, 1725, 1775),labels = c(1575, 1600, 1625, 1650, 1675, 1700, 1725, 1775)) +
   labs(tag = "C)") +
  coord_sf() +
  labs(color="Relative light \n (proportion relative \n to reference)") +
  theme_map() +
  theme(legend.position="right") +
 theme(legend.key.width=unit(0.5, "cm"),
        legend.key.height = unit(1, "cm"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
        legend.key.size = unit(5, "cm"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12))
p.lig

png("images/Field-manuscript-figs/field-manu-revised-figs/appendix8-light.png")
p.lig
dev.off()
```

```{r Table elevation, light, size - leaves}
f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- read.csv("data/outputs/combined-temp-pheno-dat/leaf-predictors.csv",
                     header = TRUE,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
  rename(Tree = SSS.tag_as, Year = year)

# preapare gounping variables
# make site a factor
f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site <- as.factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$Site) 
f_t_dat_lo19.21$Year <- as.factor(f_t_dat_lo19.21$Year)
f_t_dat_fl19.21$zone_nam_1 <- as.factor(f_t_dat_fl19.21$zone_nam_1)
# remove wonderland, union, bas1, 
f_t_dat_lo19.21 <- f_t_dat_lo19.21 %>% 
   filter(Site != "WOND", Site != "SUMA",Site != "UNIO",Site != "BAS1") 

# no variation in phenology year to year for leaves
# test with no year in the model# test with no yeayearr in the model
lo.mixed.yr <- lmerTest::lmer(jul0.5_TGLO_d ~ average_minTdep_l + trunk_di_1 + tree_heigh + Elevation + rel_light_site + (1 | Site) + (1 | Site:Tree), REML =  FALSE, data = f_t_dat_lo19.21)
lo.mixed.yr
summary(lo.mixed.yr) # Year and Site do not vary because temp, imp, dist city center, and zone are  not different by tree

sjPlot::tab_model(lo.mixed.yr,
                                  # 1. Custom predictor labels (must align with the order of coefficients)
  pred.labels = c("(Intercept)", "Temperture departure (°C)", "DBH (cm)", "Tree height (m)", "Elevation (m)", "Relative light (lumens) "),

  # 2. Custom dependent variable label
  dv.labels = c("leaf opening"),
  show.aic = TRUE,

  # 3. Prevent sjPlot from trying to auto-fetch labels from data attributes
  auto.label = FALSE
)

```
